'''Mount Moriya''' (守屋山) is a mountain with an elevation of 1,651 meters, located on the border between {{ill|Suwa, Nagano|en|Suwa, Nagano|qid=Q846338|lt=Suwa, Nagano}} and {{ill|Ina, Nagano|en|Ina, Nagano|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}} in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}.<ref name="gsi.go.jp/common/000091072">{{Cite news|url=https://www.gsi.go.jp/common/000091072.pdf|title=Revised Elevation Values for Mountains|publisher=Geospatial Information Authority of Japan|accessdate=2014-03-26}}</ref>

== Name ==
The mountain was historically known as '''Moriya Mountain''' (森山). Historical records also refer to it as '''Moriya Peak''' (守屋ヶ嶽) or '''Moriya Ridge''' (守矢が岳).<ref>Ota, Ryo, "[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/983470/122 Suwa Shrine Records Vol. 1]," 1926, pp. 225, 227.</ref>

Locals in the Suwa region often refer to the mountain range that includes Mount Moriya as "Nishiyama" (西山), meaning "Western Mountains."

== Overview ==
Situated at the northernmost part of the {{ill|Ina Mountains|ja|伊那山地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ina Mountains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11380892}}, the summit provides panoramic views of the {{ill|Akaishi Mountains|en|Akaishi Mountains|qid=Q415350|lt=Southern Alps (Japan)}}, {{ill|Kiso Mountains|en|Kiso Mountains|qid=Q1072062|lt=Central Alps (Japan)}}, {{ill|Hida Mountains|en|Hida Mountains|qid=Q1072070|lt=Northern Alps (Japan)}}, and {{ill|Yatsugatake Mountains|en|Yatsugatake Mountains|qid=Q11390433|lt=Yatsugatake Mountains}}. The mountain serves as the source of the {{ill|Sawakawa River|ja|沢川}}, which flows into {{ill|Minowa Dam|en|Minowa Dam|qid=Q11166611|lt=Lake Momiji}} before joining the {{ill|Tenryū River|arz|نهر تينريو|ceb|Tenryū-gawa (suba sa Hapon)|de|Tenryū (Fluss)|eu|Tenryū ibaia|fa|رود تنریو|fr|Tenryū-gawa|id|Sungai Tenryū|ja|天竜川|ko|덴류강|no|Tenryu (elv)|ru|Тенрю (река)|tg|Тенрю (дарё)|zh|天龍川|qid=Q13667|lt=Tenryu River}}.

The mountain is composed primarily of {{ill|green tuff|ja|緑色凝灰岩|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/green tuff|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to グリーンタフ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11300545}}, making it a geologically significant area where the {{ill|Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line|en|Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line|qid=Q906591|lt=Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line}} intersects with the {{ill|Japan Median Tectonic Line|en|Japan Median Tectonic Line|qid=Q1185053|lt=Median Tectonic Line}}.

On the eastern peak, a stone shrine—referred to in ancient maps as the "Moriya Great Minister Shrine" (守矢大臣宮)—is associated with {{ill|Moriya Shrine|ja|守屋神社}} in {{ill|Ina, Nagano|en|Ina, Nagano|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}}.<ref>Hara, Masanao, "Customs and Legends of Mount Moriya," in ''Suwa Studies'', ed. Hiroko Yamamoto, Kokusho Kankokai, 2018, pp. 133–137.</ref>

== Belief and Worship ==
[[File:守屋神社奥宮（守屋山東峰） - Mononobe no Moriya Shrine (Mt. Moriya).jpg|thumb|200px|The inner shrine and sacred rock at the eastern peak]]
Mount Moriya has long been revered as the abode of the deity {{ill|Moreya|en|Moreya|qid=Q11146526|lt=Moriya}}, also identified with {{ill|Mononobe no Moriya|en|Mononobe no Moriya|qid=Q2424736|lt=Mononobe no Moriya}}.

=== Rain Rituals ===
It is believed that when the deity of Mount Moriya is angered, rain will follow. In times of drought, locals performed rituals involving throwing the summit shrine into the valley, a practice now prevented by fences.<ref>Hara, Masanao, "Customs and Legends of Mount Moriya," in ''Suwa Studies'', ed. Hiroko Yamamoto, Kokusho Kankokai, 2018, pp. 141–143.</ref>

The saying, "When clouds gather on Moriya and the shrike cries, it’s time to sharpen the sickle," reflects the traditional use of the mountain for weather forecasting.<ref>Hara, Masanao, "Customs and Legends of Mount Moriya," in ''Suwa Studies'', ed. Hiroko Yamamoto, Kokusho Kankokai, 2018, pp. 140–141.</ref>

=== Sacred Rock Worship ===
The rock adjacent to the shrine was also venerated as a sacred site. Ancient ceremonies involved circling this rock seven times and then visiting {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}}.<ref>Hara, Masanao, "Customs and Legends of Mount Moriya," in ''Suwa Studies'', ed. Hiroko Yamamoto, Kokusho Kankokai, 2018, p. 143.</ref>
